_readme: A worked rounding example per shipped jurisdiction profile - PF-081.
Every number here was produced by the code and then written down, and the check in
tests/Support/RoundingPolicyRules.php compares the code against this file rather than
against itself. That is the whole point of committing it: a check that computed the
expected value the same way it computes the actual one asserts that multiplication is
`per_rate_group` and `per_line` are the same lines under the two bases. Every example
DIFFERS between them, deliberately - an example where they agree proves nothing about
the policy, and the check refuses one. Note the direction is not consistent: the group
figure is higher for SAR, EGP and JOD here and lower for the EUR cases, which is why
a per-line total cannot be corrected afterwards by a rounding adjustment.
`tax` is the answer for the profile as configured. If a profile's basis changes in
config/jurisdictions.php, this value changes with it and the check says so.

examples.note: EN 16931's own baseline. Three lines that round down individually and up together.
A price just under fifty, which is where a cent of drift is easiest to miss.
The Saudi standard rate. This is the example in docs/domain/tax-engine.md.
The French standard rate, on lines that total a round hundred. The per-line answer is a cent over.
A three-decimal currency. JOD has three because ISO 4217 says so, not because of Jordan's VAT rules - which is why the scale is not a per-jurisdiction setting.
